# Analysis Plan
<!-- Auto-generated by /new-analysis-plan. Edit freely, but preserve chunk IDs and status values. -->

## Project Summary
Foldseek.jl currently exposes a single low-level primitive (`foldseek(::Cmd)`) that runs the `Foldseek_jll`-bundled executable. This plan grows it into a Julia wrapper covering the `foldseek` CLI: typed, documented functions for the ~27 commands `foldseek -h` shows (the commands users actually reach for), plus a `foldseek"..."` string macro that passes any command straight through to the CLI verbatim — the escape hatch that gives access to Foldseek's remaining ~150 hidden/inherited commands without needing a typed wrapper for each one. BioJulia ecosystem interop (BioSequences.jl, FASTX.jl, BioAlignments.jl, BioSymbols.jl, MIToS.jl — the protein structure/sequence analysis toolbox at https://github.com/diegozea/MIToS.jl) is an explicit fast-follow, not part of this plan — see Open Questions.

## Language & Environment
- **Language**: Julia 1.10+ (LTS), tested against current release too
- **Key libraries**: `Foldseek_jll` (compat `"10"`); `Test` for the test suite. No BioJulia deps in this plan.
- **Environment file**: `Project.toml` (already present)
- **Project maturity target**: `releasable-package`
- **Package name(s)**: Foldseek.jl (extending the existing package, not creating a new one)
- **Extending existing package(s)**: Foldseek.jl at `/Users/carlos/git/Foldseek.jl` (this repo)

## Working stance
Intended consumer: reusable lab tool, registry-quality — docstrings, a clean public API, and passing tests are expected in every chunk, not deferred to a polish pass. Off-piste tolerance: default (record adjacent findings in Open Questions rather than pausing or ignoring).

## Target Outputs
No figures/visualization for this plan — the project's outputs are code artifacts and a coverage contract:
- `CLI_NOTES.md` (from CHUNK-001): the full enumerated `foldseek` CLI surface (subcommands + flags), which is the ground truth the rest of the plan is built against.
- A coverage table (in README or `docs/`) mapping every command `foldseek -h` shows to its wrapping Julia function, plus a documented note that `foldseek"..."` covers everything else — the durable evidence that "the whole CLI is reachable from Julia" is met, without requiring a bespoke typed wrapper per command.
- A passing, offline test suite (no network access, no dependence on real research data) — the primary way a future session or collaborator can verify the wrapper still works.
- `scripts/` end-to-end example(s) demonstrating a full workflow through the wrapper alone.

## Working knowledge
- 2026-08-16 (CHUNK-001): `foldseek -h` only shows a curated ~24-command subset. Foldseek is built on the mmseqs2 command framework (`hide_base_commands = true` in `src/foldseek.cpp`) and inherits its full 141-command table, hidden from `-h` but fully callable (confirmed: `foldseek createtsv -h`, `foldseek mvdb -h`, `foldseek version` all work). Several foldseek-specific commands are likewise `COMMAND_HIDDEN` (`version`, `structureto3didescriptor`, `scorecomplex`, ...). Enumerating "the full CLI" requires reading the upstream source command tables (`src/FoldseekBase.cpp`, `lib/mmseqs/src/MMseqsBase.cpp`), not just `-h`. Full inventory and category breakdown in `CLI_NOTES.md`.
- 2026-08-16 (CHUNK-001): `BOOL`-typed CLI options (e.g. `-a BOOL`, `--diag-score BOOL`) require an explicit `0`/`1` value passed after the flag — they are not bare presence/absence switches. CHUNK-003's dispatcher must map Julia `Bool` keyword values to `--flag 0`/`--flag 1`, not to a bare `--flag` when true and omitted when false.
- 2026-08-16 (CHUNK-001, corrected after user review): whether a command shows up in `foldseek -h` is **not** fully determined by its C++ category — e.g. `structureclusterupdate` is `COMMAND_MAIN` and `lolalign`/`easy-complexsearch` sit in categories that partly appear in `-h`, yet none of the three are actually printed by `foldseek -h`. The literal list of ~27 names printed by `foldseek -h` (recorded verbatim in `CLI_NOTES.md`) is the only reliable ground truth for "is this a typed-wrapper command," not category membership.
- 2026-08-16 (CHUNK-001, after user decision): scope for typed wrappers is now fixed at exactly the commands `foldseek -h` prints (~27; see `CLI_NOTES.md`). Everything else — hidden foldseek commands and all inherited mmseqs2 commands — is reached through the `foldseek"..."` string macro (CHUNK-005) instead of individual typed wrappers. This replaces the CHUNK-013 (blocked) / Tier-2 / Tier-3 categorization from the original CHUNK-001 pass; that categorization is superseded, not just deferred.
- 2026-08-16: the string-macro's canonical call syntax is `foldseek"easy-search q.pdb t.pdb out.m8 tmp"` (Julia's `prefix"..."` sugar for a macro named `@foldseek_str`), not `@foldseek"..."` — Julia only expands the `prefix"..."` sugar for macros whose name ends in `_str`; there is no way to make bare `@foldseek"..."` work as a non-standard string literal.

## Chunks

### CHUNK-001: cli-recon
- **Description**: Run `foldseek -h` to enumerate every module/subcommand, then `foldseek <subcommand> -h` for each to capture its flags, positional arguments, and defaults. Group subcommands by category (database management, easy-workflows, search, clustering, alignment, format conversion, utility/misc). Also inspect what minimal input Foldseek needs (PDB/mmCIF structure requirements) and propose a test-fixture strategy (bundled tiny real structures vs. inline synthetic) for later chunks to use. Write everything to `CLI_NOTES.md`, including a proposed grouping of subcommands into wrapper source files (used to scope CHUNK-005 through CHUNK-008).
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Outputs**: `CLI_NOTES.md`
- **Verification strategy**: Manual review — confirm the subcommand list against `foldseek -h` output and that the grouping is sensible.
- **Notes**: `foldseek -h` covers only ~27 of ~180 total commands; cross-checked the upstream GitHub source (`steineggerlab/foldseek`, shallow-cloned to inspect `FoldseekBase.cpp`/`MMseqsBase.cpp`) to get the authoritative full list, since there's no in-CLI way to list hidden commands. First pass proposed a Tier 1 (wrap now, ~79 commands) / Tier 2 (blocked, ~35 commands) / out-of-scope (~48 commands) split across CHUNK-005–013. After review, the user rejected that in favor of a much narrower scope: typed wrappers only for the exact ~27 commands `foldseek -h` prints, plus a `foldseek"..."` passthrough macro (CHUNK-005) for everything else. Chunks renumbered accordingly below. Test fixture recommendation unchanged: bundle `example/1tim.pdb.gz` + `example/8tim.pdb.gz` from foldseek's own repo (public-domain PDB coordinate data, ~72–84 KB gzipped, two homologous structures giving search/cluster/rbh a genuine positive hit to assert on).

### CHUNK-002: scaffold-package
- **Description**: `Project.toml`, `src/Foldseek.jl`, and `test/runtests.jl` already exist. `Foldseek_jll` is pinned via `compat = "10"`, `julia = "1.10"`. The base primitive `foldseek(args::Cmd)` runs the JLL-bundled executable and returns the `Process`.
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Notes**: Completed in commit `5a1ecf5` ("Scaffold package: thin wrapper around Foldseek_jll"), prior to this plan's creation.

### CHUNK-003: core-command-dispatcher
- **Description**: Refactor the existing `foldseek(args::Cmd)` primitive into the shared low-level dispatcher every typed subcommand wrapper below (and the CHUNK-005 macro) will call: given a subcommand name, positional args, and Julia keyword arguments, build the corresponding `Cmd` (kwargs map to `--flag value`; per Working Knowledge above, `Bool` values map to `--flag 0`/`--flag 1`, not a bare `--flag`), run it, and raise a Julia error including captured stderr on nonzero exit rather than letting `run` throw its generic `ProcessFailedException`.
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-001 (flag-naming conventions), CHUNK-002
- **Verification strategy**: Unit tests using argument-free or metadata-only invocations (e.g. `version`, `-h`) that don't require structure data.
- **Notes**:

### CHUNK-004: test-fixtures
- **Description**: Based on CHUNK-001's recon, add whatever minimal structure files or synthetic fixtures are needed for database/search/alignment tests, under `test/data/`. If real PDB/mmCIF files are bundled, record their provenance and license in a short note alongside them.
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-001
- **Verification strategy**: A smoke test that loads/parses each fixture successfully.
- **Notes**:

### CHUNK-005: foldseek-str-macro
- **Description**: A `@foldseek_str` macro (used as `foldseek"easy-search q.pdb t.pdb out.m8 tmp"`) that tokenizes its string argument the way a shell would (quoting/escaping included — reuse `Base.shell_split`, the same tokenizer Julia's own `` `cmd` `` literal uses internally) and runs it through CHUNK-003's dispatcher. This is the universal escape hatch: any command not covered by a typed wrapper (CHUNK-006 onward), including every hidden foldseek command and all ~141 commands inherited from mmseqs2, stays reachable without writing a bespoke wrapper for each one. High priority — this is what makes the narrower CHUNK-006+ scope (typed wrappers only for `foldseek -h` commands) acceptable rather than a coverage gap.
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-003
- **Verification strategy**: Unit tests comparing `foldseek"version"`-style invocations (and a case with a quoted argument containing a space) against the equivalent direct dispatcher call.
- **Notes**:
